messages:
Maya: Quick design review — new error heatmap legend + correlation ID placement. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/error-heatmap-legends (look at frame 'legend + export') :eyes:
Jonah: Nice! first pass thoughts — legend colors feel low contrast on light mode. hard to read on the palette swatch labels.
Sam: Agree on contrast. Also the gradient stops are 0/50/100 but we show counts that skew heavily right — might mislead users. Can we add min/median/max numbers under the legend?
Alex: Re: numbers — we added a small summary line in the mock: "min • median • max" under the gradient. But label copy currently says "Error intensity" which feels vague. Suggest "Errors per minute (heatmap)" or "Error density"?
Priya: Prefer "Error density (per min)" — more explicit for ops teams. Also let's avoid parentheses in the legend if we can — makes it noisy in a small panel.
Maya: Good call. What about using a short subtitle below the legend: "Avg errors/min across time buckets" — keeps the title short "Error density" and the subtitle clarifies units.
Jonah: UX nit: correlation ID column in the drilldown table — currently uses full UUID, which breaks layout. Two ideas: 1) show truncated (first 8 / last 4) with tooltip for full value; 2) show a short copy like "corr_8a3f...9c4" with copy-to-clipboard. Which do we prefer?
Sam: Definitely truncate + tooltip + copy button. We should also make the entire row keyboard-focusable so keyboard-only users can copy the ID (aria role and tabindex).
Priya: +1. Also add aria-label for the copy button: `Copy correlation ID for selected request` (or shorter?) — a11y-bot will want a concise label.
a11y-bot: Automated check: suggested aria-label length under 80 chars. Recommended: `Copy correlation ID` and add visually-hidden text when used in context: `for request at {timestamp}` to disambiguate in screenreaders.
Alex: For export actions (we have CSV/JSON export buttons inside the heatmap panel) — they sit on the right and overlap the panel header on narrow screens. Propose moving them into a kebab menu (overflow) and adding explicit keyboard shortcuts shown in tooltip.
Maya: Overflow menu sounds good. But we should surface the most common action: "Export traces (CSV)" as a primary button and hide advanced options under kebab. Everybody ok?
Jonah: Yes, but make the primary button non-destructive style. Also confirm the CSV format columns — include correlation_id, trace_id, service, timestamp, error_message, sample_payload (bool). We need a short copy in the export modal explaining sampling.
Sam: Export modal copy suggestion: `Included rows: top matching traces by error count. Sampling applied when result set > 5k.` Short and scannable.
Priya: Accessibility: ensure modal traps focus, the export confirm button has aria-disabled when action not available, and the download link has `rel="noopener"` if opening a new tab.
Maya: Quick microcopy items — prefers shorter headings in the panel: change "Trace correlation ID" -> "Correlation ID", "Export traces" -> "Export traces (CSV)" on hover only.
Alex: Small keyboard flow: hitting Enter on a focused correlation ID should copy it. Also provide `Shift+Enter` to open trace detail in a new tab. Documented in keyboard shortcuts list.
Jonah: Minor: heatmap legend tooltip example currently verbose. Proposed example content (2 lines):
```
Counts are per-minute averages. Hover a cell to see exact counts and top affected services.
Click a cell to open request drilldown.
```
Sam: That reads well. For localization keep no punctuation-heavy sentences and avoid contractions.
Priya: Contrast check: the orange stop on the gradient is failing AA when used with white text for the label. Either darken the stop or use black text on that swatch.
Maya: I'll update the swatches in Figma: darken orange by 7% and test again.
Alex: One more: on mobile the heatmap collapses into list view. Can we keep the legend sticky when scrolling the list? Users lose context otherwise.
Maya: Sticky legend for mobile is doable; probably only after we test perf. I'll add a note in the ticket: "mobile sticky legend — ensure paint cost acceptable".
Jonah: Last thing — can we standardize the phrase used across the console: "Correlation ID" vs "Trace ID" vs "Span ID". Product decision needed: Correlation ID = request-level id (user-facing), Trace ID = distributed trace id (backend), Span ID = single span. Recommend we add a glossary tooltip in the top-right help icon.
Alex: Agree. I'll draft a short glossary copy and post it here tomorrow.
Maya: Thanks all — I'll iterate the Figma file with these changes and ping when ready for final pass. :sparkles: 
Alex: :thumbsup:
Sam: :raised_hands:
Priya: :heart:
Maya: (bot) deploy-preview link updated: https://deploy-preview.redwood/heatmap-legend-1839501234
